transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-06-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Jordan (NexaHealth VP Eng), Priya (Infra), Alex (Product), Samir (Security)
Link: deck (https://redwood.example/deck/nexa-poc) | security pack (https://redwood.example/security/nexa)

Summary:
Quick onboarding sync focused on access, VPC peering, initial benchmark plan and next steps for SOC2/KMS review. Customer reported partial access done, still blocked on service account and route table settings. Redwood to run controlled benchmark and share infra snippets.

Topics: onboarding progress, access setup, VPC peering, IAM/service accounts, benchmark plan, security questions (SOC2, KMS), tuning prompts, timeline for pilot sign-off.

00:00 Speaker 1: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we can kick off, maya and carlos from redwood here
00:12 Maya: hi all yeah thanks jordan for doing the time. quick agenda: 1) access check 2) benchmark plan 3) tuning and prompts 4) security Qs and next steps
00:25 Jordan: sounds good, quick note we only have 45 so want to be concrete
00:32 Priya: status from infra side — we've created the peering request but the route tables haven't been adjusted yet, we were waiting on the exact IP ranges from you. also need the service account details for the pilot
00:47 Maya: got it, i'll drop the ip ranges and a terraform snippet in slack after this call. the ip ranges are the dedicated egress ips, i'll include both the primary region and failover region
01:03 Carlos: on the peering, a couple gotchas we've seen — make sure security groups allow the 443 egress to the redwood hosts, and if you're using managed nat the health checks can be finicky; we'll add notes
01:20 Priya: one more — do we need to open any extra ports for kv cache or anything else?
01:26 Carlos: no, just 443 for the control plane and the inference endpoints. the kayvee cache (kv cache) runs inside the runtime, it's tunneled over the same channel, so no extra ports required. sometimes people think they need extra firewall rules but it's not the case
01:45 Alex: product side — we have the golden prompts almost ready, we'll share 25 examples, also want to confirm how we trace prompt-level latency and cost in the console
01:58 Lina: in the console you'll get token-level cost breakdowns and per-request latency traces, we can show you the dashboard later in a demo, but for now carlos will run a benchmark and post the sheet with P50/P95 and token counts
02:15 Jordan: ok good. on timelines we were hoping to have a sandbox up by monday to start testing with dev traffic, is that realistic?
02:25 Maya: if priya can finish the service account and route table changes by friday then yes monday sandbox is doable
02:33 Priya: we can do friday, just need the exact ip ranges and service account json keys — do you want us to upload to our s3? are there any kms requirements?
02:45 Samir: on security — we need ensure logs are auditable, and keys are customer-managed. SOC 2 certs, iso are fine but we need details on how audit logs are exported and retention
02:58 Maya: great question, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs can be exported to your cloud logging project. i'll attach the security pack link after the call. for SOC2 our compliance team provided a full mapping doc, i'll share that too
03:15 Samir: also curious about data retention and any default retention on console? we prefer short retention for dev envs
03:24 Lina: retention is configurable per project, and dev sandboxes can be set to 7 days. we'll document the setting in the checklist
03:33 Jordan: let's talk benchmarks — carlos?
03:36 Carlos: plan is to run two tests: 1) steady-state throughput at 100 concurrent gen requests for 15 minutes, 2) latency tail test with bursty traffic to measure P95/P99. we'll run on model v1.2 (the quantized variant you asked about) and compare hosted vs dedicated configs. expected run time ~1 hour total including warmup. i'll push results to the shared spreadsheet and include cost per 1k tokens estimate
04:05 Alex: for the golden prompts we want the model to preserve privacy filters and redact pII — any tuning recommended?
04:15 Carlos: yes we'll run a small eval set with your prompts and a detector for pII and tune the temperature/top-p; also we can enable output filters and prompt engineering to reduce hallucinations. we'll note the recommended config per prompt in the results sheet
04:33 Jordan: what about failures and fallbacks? if a node is down do we automatically failover to region or to a cheaper model?
04:42 Maya: routing policies can be set to fail to a compatible variant or fallback region automatically; you can pick latency-first or cost-saver modes. for the POC we'll keep latency-first with a single-region failover to reduce complexity
04:58 Priya: for VPC peering, what about private deployment option — is private on-prem still a thing for later phases?
05:07 Maya: yes private deployment is an option but for the pilot we recommend hosted with VPC peering; private on-prem is a later-stage conversation and requires enterprise package and longer lead time
05:20 Samir: when you say customer-managed keys, is the KMS pull or push model? we prefer we retain full control of keys so provider never sees plaintext keys
05:30 Carlos: it's customer-managed KMS where keys stay in your project and we use envelope encryption — basically provider doesn't have raw keys. we'll include architecture diagram in the security doc
05:43 Jordan: ok next, can you clarify the access pattern for logs and tracing? who on our team gets RBAC and what roles we should create
05:52 Lina: we'll send recommended RBAC roles: admin (prod ops), dev (sandbox), auditor (read-only logs). you can map to SAML groups. we'll include a sample mapping in the checklist
06:10 Maya: quick note on quotas — for the pilot we'll set a soft quota to avoid surprise bills; we can increase temporarily for the benchmark then lower back
06:18 Priya: good. about the service account — do you need an IAM role with any special policies?
06:24 Carlos: yes minimal policies: write to your monitoring project for traces (if you enable), network access permissions for peering acceptance, and access to read object store if you choose to pin datasets. we'll provide exact policy JSON
06:40 Alex: on performance metrics we'll want token-level cost and per-prompt success/failure counts, can redwood tag requests with our internal request id so we can correlate?
06:52 Carlos: yep you can pass x-request-id header and it's surfaced in traces and logs. that will let you join with your product analytics
07:05 Jordan: any blockers left?
07:08 Priya: blockers: 1) ip ranges and service account details, 2) confirm firewall rules, 3) golden prompts delivered.
07:15 Maya: action items noted. i'll send infra checklist and terraform snippets, carlos will kick off benchmark once service account is in place, samir we'll set security deep-dive next wed, alex to share prompts by thursday
07:30 Samir: quick follow — can you share example of audit log format? sometimes fields are truncated in other tools
07:38 Lina: yes we'll attach an example export (json lines) in the security pack.
07:45 Jordan: ok let's recap then close
07:50 Maya: recap: 1) Maya to send infra checklist + ip ranges + terraform samples by 6/25, 2) Priya to provision service account and allowlist by 6/26, 3) Alex to deliver prompts by 6/24, 4) Carlos to run benchmark and upload results by 6/28, 5) Security deep dive scheduled for 6/30 — maya to confirm invite.
08:12 Jordan: thanks everyone, talk soon
08:15 Speaker 2: thanks, bye

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears (kayvee -> kv, redwood names sometimes capitalized weird), filler words present.
